verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own machine-authentication feature. M2M tokens authenticate calls between agents, and API keys authenticate programmatic callers such as scripts, cron jobs and partner backends, so no human needs to be in the loop. The pricing page confirms that API keys and M2M tokens are a metered platform feature. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of an OAuth client-credentials grant, detail on how M2M credentials are issued and rotated, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue machine-to-machine credentials (client-credentials flow) so backend services and agents authenticate without a human in the loop

citations.quote: API keys authenticate programmatic callers; M2M tokens authenticate calls between your agents.
An API key authenticates a known programmatic caller — a script, a cron job, a partner's backend — as a Clerk user or org.
machine authentication (API keys and machine-to-machine tokens) is a metered platform feature across plans
